key_insight: A$^3$PreCore improves the reliability of transferring brain masks into native FLAIR space by using a more robust rigid-registration strategy that is less likely to fail than standard T1-to-FLAIR alignment. It preserves the original T1-space anatomical mask while better aligning the full T1 image to FLAIR.
problem_solved: Standard rigid registration between T1 and FLAIR images can be unstable, causing inaccurate brain-mask transfer in native FLAIR space. This creates quality-control and downstream analysis issues in neuroimaging pipelines.
method: Uses a 6-degree-of-freedom rigid registration between the full bias-corrected T1-weighted image and native FLAIR.
Optimizes alignment with normalized mutual information for improved robustness.
Retains the established T1-space anatomical mask while adding extended quantitative quality control (E-QC) to assess mask extent and field-of-view coverage.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners working with medical imaging, this improves preprocessing reliability and reduces failure cases that can propagate into training or inference. More stable mask transfer means cleaner inputs, better QC, and more trustworthy downstream results.

paper_title: A$^3$PreCore: Robust Rigid Registration for Native FLAIR-Space Brain-Mask Transfer
paper_authors: Elmira Mirzabeigi, Zahra Khalilzad, Taylor Snowden-Richardson, Jesus Eduardo Lugo Arce, Jodie R. Gawryluk
